name: Question 1
problem:
$$
{y}^{″}+(3x-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)){y}^{′}+(x+1)y=0
$$

Consider the second-order homogeneous differential equation above. Let ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ be solutions, and let $W(x)$ be their Wronskian. Which differential equation must $W(x)$ satisfy?$\,$
${W}^{′}(x)=$ {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Abel's identity says that if ${y}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}$ are solutions of

$$
{y}^{″}+P(x){y}^{′}+Q(x)y=0,
$$

then their Wronskian $W(x)$ satisfies

$$
{W}^{′}(x)=-P(x)W(x).
$$

In our equation, the coefficient of ${y}^{′}$ is 

$$
P(x)=3x-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).
$$

Substituting this into Abel's identity gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{W}^{′}(x) & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-3x)W(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1

y″+(3x−sin⁡(x))y′+(x+1)y=0 Consider the second-order homogeneous differential equation above. Let y1 and y2 be solutions, and let W(x) be their Wronskian. Which differential equation must W(x) satisfy? W′(x)=
(sin⁡(x)−3x)W(x)
sin⁡(x)W(x)
(3x−sin⁡(x))W(x)
−3xW(x)
(sin⁡(x)−3x)W(x)
−(x+1)W(x)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Abel's identity says that if y1 and y2 are solutions of y″+P(x)y′+Q(x)y=0, then their Wronskian W(x) satisfies W′(x)=−P(x)W(x).

In our equation, the coefficient of y′ is P(x)=3x−sin⁡(x).

Substituting this into Abel's identity gives W′(x)=(sin⁡(x)−3x)W(x).
